why: The diff adds `+ 1` to pageCount; the consequence is that it returns one page more than the items need, and no phrasing of that appears in the diff text. Expecting the consequence rather than the `+ 1` token is deliberate: `+ 1` can be echoed straight out of the added line without understanding it, so it cannot distinguish a review that found the bug from one that quoted the hunk. The array accepts equivalent phrasings of the same finding (`extra page`, `one page too many`, …) so the case scores whether the review found it, not whether it picked one wording. `off-by-one` is deliberately NOT accepted: paired with the required `pageCount` it can be satisfied by a review that only describes the `clampPage` hunk.

The diff REPLACES `lastPage - 1` with `lastPage` — a fix. A review that reads deleted lines as current reports `lastPage - 1` as live behaviour; a review that reads it correctly says it was removed or replaced, and passes. The matcher is SENTENCE-scoped: a sentence framing the value as removed, replaced, restored or previously returned passes, a sentence with no such framing fails, and `still`/`keeps` beats a removal word in the same sentence. `expect` exists because `expect_absent` alone is satisfied by SILENCE: a review that only discussed the `pageCount` bug passed this case without ever looking at the second hunk. `clampPage` and `lastPage` are identifiers, not prose, so wording cannot false-fail a review that addresses the change; direction is scored only by `expect_absent`.
